# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I have the manual, but I can't speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I cannot reach Blind at all directly - only through Deaf, but Deaf can't speak either... wait, let me check the turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf.

So the order each round is Blind speaks, then Mute (me), then Deaf. Deaf can hear Blind's speech and see my gestures. Blind can hear (Deaf's speech from previous round) but not see. I can see nothing, hear nothing spoken to me except... wait, I "cannot speak, cannot hear" - let me recheck: Mute cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Let me re-read: Deaf cannot hear anything. Blind cannot see. Mute cannot speak.

So Mute (me) CAN hear and CAN see gestures presumably? Actually "Mute: Can read the manual. Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So I can hear and see gestures too.

Right now I have no context yet - nothing arrived. I need to wait until I know what display/light combo Deaf sees, or what Blind needs. Since I can't speak, I can only relay manual info via gestures to Deaf. But Deaf needs to tell Blind the wire color - Deaf can speak (not deaf to speaking - wait Deaf "cannot hear" but presumably can speak). So Deaf speaks to Blind.

I need Deaf to tell me the display/light combo first (via speech, since I can hear), then I gesture the resulting color to Deaf... but Deaf already knows colors visually. Actually I should gesture to Deaf the answer so Deaf can speak it to Blind.

I'll wait for info first.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2

| display \ light | green | purple | red | white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows the number 3. Light is purple. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.

I have display=3, light=purple. Looking at my manual: row 3, column purple = green. So the correct wire color is green, which is wire #5 (position 5, left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green).

I need to tell Deaf which wire position to cut, since Deaf can then speak this to Blind. I can only gesture to Deaf. I'll use gestures to encode the number 5 (the wire position), since that's what Blind needs to act on.

I'll use a simple counting gesture convention: ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3, 🖐 = 5 fingers shown... Let me use a clear scheme: number of raised fingers matching gesture symbols. I'll use ☝✌🤟✋🖐 for 1-5 (✋ has 4 meaning? Actually let's just pick single symbols per digit: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=4 (fist, not standard but I'll define), 🖐=5).

Since gestures only carry meaning if defined via speech/hearing, and Deaf cannot hear speech (Deaf cannot hear anything), I cannot pre-define this via speech to Deaf. I need to just send the gesture and hope Deaf infers, or use a self-evident count: five separate finger-count gestures isn't standard either.

Simplest: send 🖐 once to mean "5" since it's a hand with 5 fingers spread - iconic for the number 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your gesture but I do not know what it means yet. Repeating the bomb info: Display 3, Light purple, Wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. If you need me to gesture something to Blind, tell me in speech what symbols to use and I will relay them as gestures, since Blind can see gestures from me too.
Blind says to Mute: I am ready to cut wires but I need instructions. Please tell me the manual's conditions - what determines which wire is safe. I can only feel wire positions 1 through 5, nothing else.

Now I understand the channel structure better. Blind can hear speech (from Deaf) and feel wires but not see gestures. Deaf can see gestures and speak, but cannot hear anything (so Deaf can't hear Blind or me speaking - but wait, I can't speak at all). Deaf can see my gestures, and Deaf can speak to Blind.

So the path is: Manual (me) → gesture to Deaf → Deaf speaks to Blind.

I confirmed: display 3, light purple → manual says green. Wire 5 is green. So Blind should cut wire 5.

I need to get "5" across via gesture to Deaf unambiguously. Deaf said they'll relay gestures as gestures to Blind, but Blind can't see gestures! So that won't work directly for numbers - Deaf needs to convert my gesture into spoken words for Blind.

I should establish a simple counting convention: I'll send five identical gesture symbols to represent the count 5, since that's unambiguous without prior agreement - Deaf can count the number of symbols I send.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
